statement: Along a decreasing chain of finite sets, |F 0| = |F N| + the sum of the gains.
If every non-terminal cube has a strictly larger cube with slack no larger, slack is nonnegative at every cube.
no_minCE follows from 0 <= Phi(0) in every minimal counterexample.
If the certificate game on the lifted outputs is won, disjoint lifted classes exist, and there is no minimal counterexample.
Local cube or one-point step at every cube with positive base gives no minimal counterexample.
A minimal counterexample has no gate-saving rewiring.
The 67-gate circuit with 4 NOT gates is correct and has 5 witness gates (base 6), in the kernel; not yet tied to the project's Circuit.eval.
Maximum principle: on states with a rank, if every state of negative value has a state of smaller rank with value no larger, no value is negative (descent is needed only at negative states).
Chain to the sorry: a mixed slack f with f ∅ ∅ = slack gates S ∅ and descent at its negative states gives 0 ≤ Phi gates S 0, hence no_minCE; the descent hypothesis is not proved.
If slack ≥ 0 at every cube then 0 ≤ Phi gates S p for 0 ≤ p ≤ 1.
Averaged descent: if the sum over the free points of the one-point changes is ≤ 0 at every negative cube and the full cube is not negative, no cube is negative.
Layer 1: for every row r < 2^n, bit r of SearchCheck's table of wire k equals the pointwise evaluation Circ.wiresAt C r at wire k (inputs via varTT_testBit, NOT via the all-ones mask).
Layer 2: correctB C = true implies that at every input vector r < 2^n every output wire of C carries the OR of the bits of r over its set (no hypothesis on the set elements).

Layer 3: the pointwise evaluation is the project's Circuit.wires on C.toGates (wiresAt_eq_wires), so correctB C = true and sets.length ≤ outs.length give exactly the correctness hypothesis of L_meta_951 for gates := C.toGates, S := C.setFin, out w := C.outs.getD w 0 (the gate hypothesis is toGates_wf); instance first_ast_tiny_concrete for asteroid/examples/first.ath.

Layer 4: under SetsOk (sets without repeated points, points < n), asteroid's orWitnessAt C (maskOf Q) equals (F2 C.toGates C.setFin Q).card and baseAt equals baseDQ C.setFin ∅ Q, so slackNonnegAll C = true gives baseDQ ≤ |F2| at every Q, and slackGe C 0 0 = true gives MUF2 and Σ(|S|-1) ≤ gates for that circuit.

Not proved: any project counterpart of asteroid's witnessCount / hasWitness (witness gates of any type; F2 counts OR gates only), and asteroid.py does not yet emit the corollaries correctB_sound_project / slackNonnegAll_sound (with a SetsOk proof) into the generated modules.
asteroid restates every correctness and slack claim of a program in the project's definitions (Circuit.eval, F2, baseDQ) in a second generated module; built for all four example programs.
A circuit literal with well-formed sets whose kernel check slack(c) >= 0 succeeds is not a counterexample to the Theorem (IsCE) and not a minimal one (MinCE), for any output wires.
The Lean slack of ContinuousAttach on the translated circuit at a cube Q equals asteroid's orWitnessAt minus baseAt at the mask of Q.
If the kernel check 'forall cubes slack(c) >= 0' succeeds, the product-measure average Phi(p) of the slack is nonnegative for every p in [0,1] (and the slack is nonnegative at every cube).
Chain sum for F2 and for asteroid's count: along any increasing chain of cubes, the count at the start is the count at step N plus the number of gates lost at each step.

hypsB is a kernel-decidable checker whose success gives the hypotheses of L_meta_951 other than correctness (sets of at least 2 points, pairwise intersections of at most 1 point, at most one NOT gate in both the index form and the iota form) for C.setFin and C.toGates.

A circuit literal passing correctB and hypsB with fewer gates than the base is a counterexample (IsCE), yields a minimal counterexample, and refutes the statement of L_meta_951 (copied verbatim as LMeta951Stmt): asteroid's hunt is a formal search for counterexamples.

If there is no minimal counterexample (taken as a hypothesis, not used as a theorem), or if the statement of L_meta_951 holds, every circuit literal passing correctB and hypsB has base at most its number of gates, with no further work.

On the diagonal r = 0 the mixed evaluator is the proved one: baseMixed C q 0 = baseAt C q, the naive mixed witness test at (q,0) is hasWitnessAt at q, and if the kernel check naiveAgrees C succeeds then mslackVal C q 0 = orWitnessAt C q - baseAt C q (and mslackGe C q 0 k = slackGe C q k) at every cube q < 2^n.

Not done: the bit-parallel hasWitnessMixed equals hasWitnessMixedNaive for every circuit and state (needs the soundness of the mask V and of the shifted tables, about the size of AsteroidSound layer 1); mslackVal_zero therefore takes it per circuit from the kernel check naiveAgrees. Mixed slack off the diagonal has no Lean counterpart (no mixed F2(Q,R) is defined).

The example instances (tiny correct/concrete/slack/setsOk, fano hypsB) now live in AsteroidInstances.lean; AsteroidSound, AsteroidSound2 and AsteroidCheap no longer import the generated Asteroid_first.
LMeta951Stmt is definitionally the type of L_meta_951 (type-checked, no drift possible); the pin is on the allow-list.
kstep_of_slack_nonneg instantiated with slack_nonneg_of_slackNonnegAll for the literal tiny of first.ath.

Dropping 0 < gates.length from hypsB not done: the Asteroid_edges claim nogate_claim4 (hypsB nogate = false, another seat) relies on that conjunct, and L_meta_951's iota hypothesis needs a gate; a no-gate-implies-incorrect lemma was not attempted.
